method: 4 adversarial lenses (evidence/engine/courts/charter) + verifying judge, 108 code reads, opus-5
verdict: BUILD-WITH-CHANGES — the architecture survives, the drafted mechanism does not. Masters as regime-gated entities that accumulate proven conditions is sound and charter-aligned (NORTH_STAR.md:48, "at most a regime portfolio of 2-4 proven strategies"). But three of the six sections must be REPLACED, not patched: §1's merge vocabulary and clock-restart, §3's calendar cadence cap, and §4's reuse of the auto_* rollback machinery. Step 1 as drafted ("seeded masters, behaviour-identical") is DO-NOT-BUILD — I verified it is provably false: a rename silently drops each anchor's pool, trigger-contract, structure and exit bindings, and `_tuned()` returns None so `sandbox_proactive_lab.py:1145-1149` falls back to stop 50 / trig 50 / give 0.20, whose own comment reads "the -50 stop sat inside bear whipsaw range and cost a third of the measured edge". The one idea in the findings set that rescues the whole design is evidence-lens finding 3's observation, which I verified: AND-only merging means each merged cohort is a strict SUBSET of the pre-merge trade set, so every counterfactual condition-set is already computable over trades the master has recorded. Retroactive re-scoring replaces clock-restart, and the accrual problem collapses from fatal to manageable. Timing helps: §7 already queues this behind proof Phases B/C, so none of this is urgent and nothing needs shipping half-fixed.
required_before_build: MERGE THE WHOLE TESTED UNIT, NOT THE PREDICATE. A roster name binds seven things, and the spec captures one. Verified: _rg_need regime map (sandbox_proactive_lab.py:2471-2472); the market-level _mkt20<0 hoist for DIP_CONVEXITY/DIP_CONF_MILD (:2478-2481); _CALLS_ONLY free check (:2495); the candidate POOL — _PRICEY_CANDS[:14] for DIP_CONF_MILD/BULL_DIP_X vs _FULL_CANDS[:16] vs candidates[2:12] (:2482-2485); the _PROBE_CONTRACT trigger-contract override (:2507-2510); PROBE_STRUCT/PROBE_EXITS via _tuned() (:410-412, :418-431); and the tuner's key space (scripts/tuner_apply.py:36-39, scripts/glide_sim.py:37-45). Note BULL_DIP_X's lambda contains NO regime test at all (:2418-2420) — its BULL gate exists ONLY in _rg_need. Each master's spec block must carry conditions, free_preconditions, pool, contract_mode (trigger vs synthesized), struct, exits and a tuner_alias, with the roster loop reading them from the block instead of the name-keyed dicts. Where a probe's proven edge is not representable in the merge vocabulary, the merge is REFUSED as 'not representable' — never approved as its filter shadow wearing the source probe's t-stat. Consequence to write down: §1's claim 'merges are data commits, never code edits' becomes false and must be struck.

SEPARATE FREE FROM COSTLY PREDICATES BEFORE THE SWEEP. probe_filter is called at sandbox_proactive_lab.py:1257, AFTER collect_metadata at :1251, so every predicate evaluation costs a full sensor sweep against a hard 10-attempt cycle budget (:2467, :2490). The comment at :2456-2463 records the incident this repeats verbatim: 'pools burn 10 attempts each without entering, cycle time blew past the dispatch interval, and every run from 17:40Z was cancelled by its successor'. Because exactly two of three masters are always in the wrong regime, this is two trading days in three, not a tail case. Regime, market-level and candidate.* conditions must be evaluated before `_att += 1` at :2511, in the same slot as the existing :2473/:2495 hoists; spec load REFUSES a master declaring no free precondition. MOT must assert the collect_metadata CALL COUNT is zero for the two wrong-regime masters on a fixture day — not a log line.

WRITE THE FAIL-POLARITY INTO THE CONTRACT BEFORE ANY EVALUATOR CODE. fade_book.spy_regime() returning None is designed and reachable: the staleness guard at fade_book.py:38-41 blanks the bar list on any Alpaca hiccup. The codebase ships BOTH conventions for that same signal — fail-CLOSED at sandbox_proactive_lab.py:2473 and in the isinstance guards at :2373/:2388-2391, fail-OPEN eight lines from the same function at fade_book.py:111-115 ('Fail-open: unknown regime -> allow'). Whoever writes the evaluator has a coin flip with house precedent on both sides, and fail-open means one SPY-bars outage makes all three masters pass simultaneously and contaminates three evidence clocks with the one cohort guaranteed unrepresentative. Rule: every condition yields strict True/False; None, type mismatch, missing path, unknown path, unknown op, or any raised exception yields False and skips the master. Whitelist lives as a Python literal, never in the spec. State the availability consequence explicitly — an SPY-bars outage zeroes the whole regime portfolio for that day, alarmed, not surprising.

DO NOT REUSE auto_* FOR ROLLBACK — IT CRASHES AND TAKES THE DEMOTION RATCHET WITH IT. Verified: the demotion sweep scans only keys starting with 'auto_' (scripts/sunday_boundary.py:209), so merge records inside masters.* are invisible to it; and if you write an auto_ marker instead, the revert does `sect, key = path.split('.')` (:234-236), a two-level unpack that raises ValueError on `masters.BULL.conditions`. That exception is caught by the single blanket `except Exception as _de` at :246-247 wrapping the ENTIRE loop, and because the json.dump/commit sit at :241-245 AFTER the loop inside the same try, one malformed record does not merely skip itself — it discards every revert computed in that pass and permanently disables demotion for every promoted key, with the only symptom the line 'demotion check skipped: ValueError'. Also verified: records are date-keyed singletons (:376, :537, :587), so two merges on one UTC date silently destroy each other's prev state. Required: masters get their own append-only merge store with monotone integer merge_id (never date-keyed) and their own rollback routine; the existing sweep gets per-record try/except with a loud skip line, which is worth doing regardless of masters.

REPLACE CLOCK-RESTART WITH RETROACTIVE RE-SCORING, AND THE CALENDAR CADENCE CAP WITH AN EVIDENCE CADENCE. Two verified halves. (a) The clock does not exist on this path: _clock is applied to MENU shadow books only (scripts/sunday_boundary.py:283-288 with the filter at :477), while the probe court builds day-means with NO clock filter — `shared = sorted(d for d in dm if d in ctrl_u)` at :351 is all-time. Ship as drafted and merges restart nothing, so the court credits a merge for returns the new condition would have EXCLUDED. (b) Implement it properly and masters die of youth: the bar needs >=8 days SHARED with EXEC_BASELINE (:352) and then drops the best AND worst before the t-test (:364), while masters are regime-gated subsets of their anchors' day supply and every AND-merge narrows further. Fix: log the full predicate vector on every master fill at entry (one record per contract, carrying which conditions it passed, regime, and the exit config in force), then re-score condition sets over the master's own recorded trades — valid because AND-merges are pure filters, so post-merge trades are a strict subset of pre-merge ones. Merge cadence gates on a COMPLETED verdict since the last merge, never on a month. Rollback removes the WORST-contributing merge by marginal contribution, not the newest. Forbid batch application of stint-queued merges — a merge that cannot be attributed is not evidence.

KILL THE LOST-WRITE CLASS ON THE SPEC BEFORE ENTRY CONDITIONS LIVE THERE. Every spec writer does json.dump then `git pull -q --rebase -X ours && git push -q` — scripts/sunday_boundary.py:243-245, :380-382, :543-545, :592-594 and scripts/tuner_apply.py:196-199 — while the engine box pulls the same file with `-X theirs` (scripts/engine_watch.sh:58, :75, :104). During a rebase 'ours' is the UPSTREAM side, so a conflicting hunk silently discards the local edit; `-q` hides it and the script then telegrams success. This is not theoretical and the repo already says so: scripts/merge_logs.py:10-11 states 'rebase inverts ours/theirs', and its docstring records the 2026-08-12 NVDA orphan where exactly this class lost a trade record. Three writers read-modify-write one whole-file JSON with no lock (sunday_boundary reloads it fresh at :207, :263, :299 and writes at :242 and :379). The only standing watchdog is 'spec parses' (scripts/freshness_sentinel.py:97), a json_ok check that passes on every one of these outcomes. Required: one writer helper, never `-X ours` on the spec, and after push re-read from origin and assert the merged condition is present BEFORE writing merge_history and BEFORE sending the ACK telegram — the verify-after-push pattern already exists at scripts/telegram_commands.py:50-56. Upgrade the sentinel from 'parses' to 'conditions fingerprint == last ACKed fingerprint' per master.

GIVE THE ACK A PROPOSAL IDENTITY, AN EXPIRY, AND A REVALIDATION. No ACK surface exists. scripts/telegram_commands.py:62-106 is the only inbound channel: a text.startswith chain over /halt /resume /flatten /cancelflatten /status, authenticated by chat-id equality alone (:79), with its de-dup offset in a $HOME state file whose bare except resets it to {'offset': 0} (:66-70). Every command it carries today is FAIL-SAFE; an ACK would be the first PERMISSIVE mutation on that channel, writing new entry conditions into a live master. Lose that state file and getUpdates(offset=1) re-serves up to 24h of messages — idempotent for /halt, a double merge for an ACK. Required: proposals become records (proposal_id, master, condition, exact evidence window, spec_version, hash of the master's current config), the ACK carries the id only, and the boundary REFUSES if the id is already in merge_history, if the config hash moved since issue, if the bar fails on the CURRENT day set, or if age > 7 days. This matters because the anti-cube law at scripts/sunday_boundary.py:248-257 exists precisely to stop a verdict being applied to a configuration that no longer exists.

INHERIT THE STARVATION INTERLOCKS THE MERGE PATH CURRENTLY SKIPS. Every AND-merge is restrictive by construction, and the boundary already blocks RESTRICTIVE promotions while starving — but only for MENU books (RESTRICTIVE set at scripts/sunday_boundary.py:140, applied at :471), and the per-leg throughput floor keys on ['FADE'] + probe.promoted (:146, :161-167), which is currently empty. LIVE_WIRED (:518-522), the guard that exists because of the spec-keys-the-engine-never-read breakdown (BREAKDOWNS.md:218-224), also covers only the MENU path — masters.* would bypass it entirely. Required: replay each proposed predicate over the master's own recorded fills and REFUSE the merge if it removes more than a set fraction of them or pushes projected time-to-verdict past one quarter; register masters in the per-leg floor so a starved master pages and auto-blocks further merges; ban md.macro.* and md.regime_stack.* from merge predicates — market-level gates delete whole DAYS, which is the unit the bar counts, and the engine already hoists exactly those out of the candidate loop for that reason (sandbox_proactive_lab.py:2478-2481). A market-level idea is a REGIME definition, not a condition.

ROUTE THE SEAT PATH AND THE MERGE PATH APART, PRE-REGISTERED. reports/proof_account_build_contract_2026-09-06.md:32-35 pins seating to exactly one place — 'SEATING fires EXCLUSIVELY in the probe-court PROMOTE branch' — and §3 of this design generates merge proposals from the same branch on the same bar, so one passing probe can both take a Proof seat as itself and inject its condition into a master that is itself a seat candidate. In a 2-4 seat portfolio that is two seats backed by ONE eight-day sample, which NORTH_STAR.md:48 forbids in terms ('never riding another's evidence'). Note the promote loop also has no one-per-run guard (scripts/sunday_boundary.py:335-386), unlike the MENU branches at :528 and :576, so with two same-regime probes passing together, position in probe.priority decides the merge — order, not evidence. Required: a probe is declared seat-candidate OR merge-source when it enters probe.priority, recorded in the spec; ranking on published trimmed t, never list order; and a master holding a proof seat freezes ALL mutation including rollback — if the court wants to roll back a merge on a seated master, that unseats it via the contract's item-8 machinery (:43-45), it does not quietly edit a live stint. §5's 'queued merge applied after a passed stint' must not stand as drafted: NORTH_STAR v1.7 freezes each seat's capture denominator in writing AT seating, so a post-stint merge changes the strategy while real capital is staked against a denominator measuring a config that no longer exists.

BUILD REAL COVERAGE — THE §6 CHECKS AS DRAFTED ARE VACUOUS. The only roster assertion in the harness is a source-string grep (v11_mot_harness.py:1081-1085, `'"WINNER_PROFILE"' in _lab_src`), and it becomes meaningless the moment the roster lives in JSON; a grep for probe/roster coverage across the harness finds nothing else, so the roster loop has never been exercised behaviourally by MOT at all. Seed-equivalence must be a behavioural fixture replay, not predicate equality: frozen candidate set plus frozen md through both the anchor path and the master path, asserting identical entered OCC, contract count, limit price, struct and exit triple. Add: each op x {None, str-vs-num, missing key, unknown path, unknown op} returns False and does not raise; empty/missing conditions refuses to trade AND emits a loud stand-down line plus telegram (the precedent is scripts/sunday_boundary.py:322-327 — an empty track is a state the owner must always see, never infer); two merges on one UTC date leave two recoverable records; a 3-segment revert path round-trips; a merged condition survives a simulated conflicting push.
open_owner_decisions: CONSOLIDATION vs ACCRUAL SPEED — the central trade, and it needs your number, not our intuition. A master is regime-gated, so its day supply is a strict subset of its anchor's, and each AND-merge narrows it further, while the bar wants >=8 days SHARED with the control and then throws away the best and worst (scripts/sunday_boundary.py:352, :364). Masters therefore reach verdicts STRICTLY SLOWER than the probes they replace. What they buy is the charter's own non-goal — 'not a strategy supermarket' (NORTH_STAR.md:48). Options: (a) build masters and accept roughly one verdict per quarter for BULL and multi-month for BEAR; (b) skip masters and instead cull the 8-name probe.priority roster competing for a hard 10-attempt cycle budget (sandbox_proactive_lab.py:2467) — that raises every survivor's fill rate immediately with zero new subsystem and zero clock resets; (c) cull first, masters later. We should publish the measured accrual table for (a) and (b) from origin data before you choose.

MASTER_BEAR AT ALL — bear regimes were about 13% of the last two years by the spec's own v2.4_note, and reports/shadow_lab/breaker.jsonl records 20 bear days in all of 2026 across 3 episodes. A bear master's verdict is a multi-month instrument arriving in bursts, and by §4's own rule a merge into it restarts everything. Options: (a) build all three masters as drafted; (b) build BULL and MILD, leave bear as the single named DIP_CONVEXITY strategy until bear-day supply justifies a master; (c) build BEAR but exempt it from merges entirely — a frozen bear entity, tuned only.

THE MERGE UNIT — predicate-only or whole-config bundle. Predicate-only keeps §1's clean claim that merges are data commits and never code edits, but it drops the half of every anchor's edge that lives in pool selection, trigger-contract override and exit shape, which is where fade_book_spec.json's own evidence notes locate it (dip_conf_mild: 'the edge lives in EXPENSIVE trigger contracts... measured ON THE TRIGGER CONTRACT'). Whole-config is honest but the 'data commits, never code edits' safety claim has to be struck and the whitelist grows to cover selectors. A third option: allow predicate-only merges but require any non-representable idea to arrive as its own probe and stay one.

ACK CEREMONY AND SEATED-MASTER MUTATION. Two calls. (a) Does a merge ACK carry the same weight as the first-promotion owner-ACK gate in reports/proof_account_build_contract_2026-09-06.md:34-35, or a lighter one? (b) When a master holding a proof seat needs a merge rolled back, does that UNSEAT it (our recommendation — it goes back to court for a fresh case with a newly frozen capture denominator) or does the rollback apply mid-stint? §5 freezes merges but says nothing about rollbacks, and rollback is currently the one mutation path left open on a live stint. Either answer is defensible; both spend against the £2,500 lifetime cap, so it is yours.

THREE LIVE DEFECTS THIS REVIEW EXPOSED THAT MASTERS DID NOT CAUSE — fix now, or fix inside the masters build? (1) scripts/tuner_apply.py:191-192 writes exit glides with no auto_* marker, so the anti-cube clock and frozen_keys at scripts/sunday_boundary.py:264-279 cannot see a Friday glide — verdicts are being earned today against configurations that changed under them. (2) The blanket except at scripts/sunday_boundary.py:246-247 wrapping the whole demotion loop is a single point of failure for the entire ratchet, independent of masters. (3) `-X ours` on every spec push can silently discard a write that the telegram then reports as applied. All three are cheap, all three are load-bearing for masters, and (1) and (3) are quietly costing evidence integrity right now.

QUIET_TAPE was CULLED on 2026-09-01 (sandbox_proactive_lab.py:2361-2362, '-$1,005 over its era, no positive stretch - roster slot freed for the grid probes'), so it is not evidence about the current roster's fill behaviour. Same staleness caveat as above applies to the other two counts. Conclusion unchanged; the numbers are struck.

CORRECTED, NOT REJECTED — charter lens and evidence lens both claim 'of the three named seeds, only BULL_DIP is expressible as pure data predicates' and therefore that masters should be scoped to BULL_DIP alone. The premise is imprecise. DIP_CONF_MILD's roster lambda (sandbox_proactive_lab.py:2387-2392) IS fully expressible in the whitelisted vocabulary — regime, macro.distance_to_sma20_pct, regime_stack.market_spy_dist_pct, flow_type. What is not expressible is its POOL (_PRICEY_CANDS[:14], :2483) and its TRIGGER-CONTRACT override (_PROBE_CONTRACT, :2507-2510). The distinction changes the fix: the answer is not 'scope masters to one anchor', it is 'the merge unit must be the whole config bundle'. Folded into required-before-build item 1. BULL_DIP_X is the genuinely broken case — its lambda has no regime test at all (:2418-2420).

DOWNGRADED — charter lens, 'the owner's core motivation, faster evidence accrual, is not merely unmet, it is reversed'. The arithmetic is right and I have kept it, but the motive is imported, not evidenced. reports/regime_masters_design_2026-09-09.md nowhere claims speed; §1 states the goal as consolidation — 'uniformly well-rounded accumulations of everything every probe has proven' — which serves the charter's 'not a strategy supermarket' non-goal at NORTH_STAR.md:48. A hostile room would break the finding on that. The slower-verdict COST is real and belongs to the owner as a priced trade-off, not as a gotcha about his intentions.

DOWNGRADED — evidence and charter lenses, '§3 mentions no throughput check anywhere' / 'the design has no accounting of it'. The design's own open-questions block flags it first: line 62, 'AND-only merge semantics: too restrictive? (Each AND narrows the funnel - throughput.)'. It is deferred to the panel, not overlooked. That does not make it safe — the interlocks genuinely are not inherited and that finding stands — but the framing must be 'the draft defers this and must not' rather than 'the draft ignores this'.

CONTEXT, NOT A MASTERS BLOCKER — courts lens, 'the probe-court class has NO demotion path today: the demotion loop scans auto_ keys only, so nothing ever re-checks a promo_* entry'. Verified true (scripts/sunday_boundary.py:209 vs :376), but it is a pre-existing gap in the probe court that this design inherits rather than creates. Worth fixing; not a reason to refuse the masters build. The related claim that IS a masters blocker — `if st_ in promoted: continue` at :336 means a promoted master is never re-judged, so §4's 'masters are judged like any probe' stops exactly when it matters — is kept and folded into the rollback and coverage items.

raw_findings.title: Fail-polarity of the evaluator is unspecified, and the codebase already ships BOTH polarities for the same signal
raw_findings.attack: fade_book.spy_regime() returning None is a designed, reachable state, not a hypothesis: the staleness guard at fade_book.py:38-41 blanks the bar list on any Alpaca hiccup and val stays None. Today that fails CLOSED for every regime probe (sandbox_proactive_lab.py:2473 `if _rg_need and fade_book.spy_regime() != _rg_need: continue`, and the same == comparison inside each lambda at 2372/2379/2387). But eight lines away, fade_book.py:111-115 documents the OPPOSITE convention in a comment for the same function: 'Fail-open: unknown regime -> allow'. The design (section 1-2) says only 'filter = regime match AND all spec conditions true' and names one MOT case ('unknown-path rejection') without saying what is rejected - the condition or the master. Whoever writes the evaluator has a 50/50 coin flip with house precedent on both sides. If it lands fail-open, one SPY-bars outage makes the regime condition vacuous and MASTER_BULL, MASTER_MILD and MASTER_BEAR all pass simultaneously: three books with opposite theses take fills on the same day, and three evidence clocks are contaminated at once with the one cohort that is guaranteed unrepresentative. The same coin flip governs every md.* path: a null distance_to_sma20_pct makes `None < 0` raise, and a broad try/except returning True drops the narrowing condition and widens the funnel silently - the current lambdas fail closed on exactly this via their isinstance guards (2373, 2388-2391). A second, quieter variant: if the roster is built FROM the spec, a merge that drops or renames the masters block removes three strategies with zero alarm; the boundary then reads zero fills as 'HOLD, insufficient virgin days' forever rather than 'the strategy vanished' - the exact silent-empty state the owner already banned once at sunday_boundary.py:322-327.
raw_findings.fix: Write the polarity into the spec contract before any code: every condition evaluates to strict True/False, and None, type-mismatch, missing path, unknown path, unknown op, or any raised exception yields False for that condition, which skips the master. No condition may ever evaluate True by default. The regime term is not a generic condition - it binds to the hoisted pre-check that already fails closed at 2473. Whitelist of paths and ops lives as a literal in Python, never in the spec, and MOT asserts it is a source literal. MOT cases: each op x {None, str-vs-num, missing key, unknown path, unknown op} returns False and does not raise; masters block missing/empty/conditions-key-absent all refuse to trade AND emit a loud stand-down line plus telegram (the 322-327 precedent); spy_regime()==None stands all three masters down. State the availability consequence in the design: with a regime portfolio of three regime-gated masters, an SPY-bars outage zeroes the whole portfolio for that day - that is correct and must be the stated, alarmed behaviour, not a surprise.

raw_findings.title: 'Seeded == anchor behaviour, day one changes nothing' is false: a probe's identity is seven name-keyed code bindings and the spec captures only one
raw_findings.attack: The design migrates the filter lambda into spec conditions and asserts behavioural identity. But a roster name today also binds: (1) the regime pre-check map `_rg_need` (2471-2472); (2) the market-level `_mkt20 < 0` hoist for DIP_CONVEXITY/DIP_CONF_MILD (2478-2481); (3) `_CALLS_ONLY` free candidate check (2454-2455); (4) the candidate POOL - `_PRICEY_CANDS[:14]` for DIP_CONF_MILD/BULL_DIP_X vs `_FULL_CANDS[:16]` vs `candidates[2:12]` (2482-2485); (5) the `_PROBE_CONTRACT` trigger-contract override (2507-2510); (6) PROBE_STRUCT/PROBE_EXITS and `_tuned(_ACTIVE_PROBE['name'], ...)` (410-412, 425, 471); (7) the tuner's own key space - INCUMBENT_POOL in tuner_apply.py:36-38 and STRATS in glide_sim.py:37-45. Rename DIP_CONF_MILD to MASTER_MILD with an identical predicate and the master buys a SYNTHESIZED 4%-OTM/35-DTE contract instead of the trigger contract, because 2483 and 2507 both key on the literal string. The spec's own evidence note says the edge 'lives in EXPENSIVE trigger contracts ... measured ON THE TRIGGER CONTRACT' (fade_book_spec.json:155). So the 'behaviour-identical' step 1 would quietly move MASTER_MILD onto a different instrument than the one its entire prior is built on, while the merge_history records DIP_CONF_MILD as its seed - the cleanest possible way to launder a changed bet as an unchanged one. Same rename also orphans it from tuner_apply/glide_sim, so its exits stop gliding and the Friday pass silently HOLDs a strategy that no longer exists under that key. The design's proposed check cannot catch any of this: predicate equality compares filters, and the existing roster MOT is a source-string grep (v11_mot_harness.py:1081-1085, `'"WINNER_PROFILE"' in _lab_src`) which becomes vacuous the moment the roster lives in JSON.
raw_findings.fix: Step 1 migrates the whole bundle, not the filter: each master's spec block carries conditions, free_preconditions, pool, contract_mode (trigger vs synthesized), struct, exits, and a tuner_alias; the roster loop reads pool/contract_mode/struct/exits from the block instead of the name-keyed dicts, and tuner_apply/glide_sim resolve strategies through the alias so the glide history survives the rename. Seed-equivalence must be a BEHAVIOURAL fixture replay, not predicate equality: feed a frozen candidate set + frozen md through both the anchor path and the master path and assert identical entered OCC, contract count, limit price, struct and exit triple - byte-identical records. Note the harness gap while building it: the probe roster block is gated on fade_book.active() at 2327 and the MOT runs FORCE_OFF (v11_mot_harness.py:1098), so the roster loop has never been exercised end-to-end by MOT - the fixture must construct that path explicitly, or the whole coverage claim in design section 6 is a check on code that never runs.

raw_findings.attack: probe_filter is called at sandbox_proactive_lab.py:1257, which is AFTER collect_metadata at 1251 - every predicate evaluation costs a full sensor sweep. The cycle budget is 10 attempts (2467, 2490). The comment block at 2456-2463 records what happens when a rare-filter probe is evaluated inside enter_proactive_set: 'pools burn 10 attempts each without entering, cycle time blew past the dispatch interval, and every run from 17:40Z was cancelled by its successor (the 08-19/08-20 churn class)'. The fix then was to hoist the regime gate to 2473 and the calls check to 2495 as FREE pre-checks - both hardcoded on probe names. The design's masters are named MASTER_BULL/MASTER_MILD/MASTER_BEAR and express the regime as a spec condition, so unless something new is built they are absent from `_rg_need` and `_CALLS_ONLY` and their regime term is evaluated post-sweep. On any BULL day, MASTER_BEAR and MASTER_MILD each walk their pool paying a sweep per name until the 10 attempts are gone; the fade book and every other probe get nothing, and the cycle overruns the dispatcher. This is not a tail case - it is two thirds of every trading day by construction, because exactly two of the three masters are always in the wrong regime. It compounds with the design's AND-only merge law: each merge narrows the funnel monotonically, so a master's pass rate falls every month while its attempt cost per candidate stays flat, and after a few merges it can hold a roster slot, burn budget, and still be undecidable by the court forever. Separately, the starved-cycle telemetry the panel relies on is already lying: line 2535 prints '{_att} of 6 attempts used' while the budget checked at 2467/2490 is 10.

The roster loop evaluates all FREE conditions before `_att += 1` at 2511, in the same slot as the existing 2473/2495 hoists, and only sweeps when they pass. Spec load REFUSES a master that declares no free precondition. MOT: on a fixture BULL day, MASTER_BEAR and MASTER_MILD cause zero collect_metadata calls (assert the call count, not a log line); a master with an md.*-only condition list is rejected at load. Fix the 'of 6' message to read the actual budget constant. Add a throughput floor to the merge path: a merge proposal that would drop the master's modelled fill rate below the rate needed to reach 8 virgin days inside the evidence window is refused, not ACKed - otherwise the AND-only law converges every master on never trading and the courts never get to speak.

raw_findings.title: The spec write path has no round-trip verification, no lock, and a conflict policy that silently discards - promoting it from exit knobs to entry conditions inherits all three
raw_findings.attack: Every spec writer does json.dump then `git add fade_book_spec.json && git commit -qm ... && git pull -q --rebase -X ours && git push -q` (tuner_apply.py:196-199; sunday_boundary.py:242-245, 379-382, and the challenger sites at 541/590). Three defects, each harmless-ish for exit knobs and load-bearing for entry conditions. (a) During a rebase, `-X ours` resolves conflicts in favour of the branch being rebased ONTO - upstream - so a conflicting hunk in the spec silently discards the local write; `-q` hides it, and the script then telegrams 'MERGE APPLIED' while main is unchanged. The owner ACKed a condition that is not live. (b) `-X` resolves per hunk, so a partial splice can produce a conditions list that neither side ever wrote and that is still valid JSON. This is not theoretical here: v10_lab.yml:99-101 records the 2026-08-24 incident where 'a rebase -X splice pushed syntactically invalid JSON'. That workflow added a validation gate - for proactive_sandbox_logs.json only. fade_book_spec.json has no such gate. Syntactically invalid at least fails closed to OFF via fade_book.py:59-64; a spliced-but-valid conditions list trades a shape nobody approved, at the next engine checkout, with merge_history asserting otherwise. (c) Three independent writers read-modify-write one file with no lock or compare-and-swap - sunday_boundary alone re-loads it fresh at 207, 263 and 299 and writes at 242 and 379 - so a concurrent tuner_apply run drops one of them entirely. Today that loses a glide step; with masters it can resurrect a pre-merge conditions list or erase an ACKed merge. The only standing watchdog is 'spec parses' (freshness_sentinel.py:97), a json_ok check that passes on every one of these outcomes.

Take a lock (or make the merge path Sunday-only and provably disjoint from the Friday tuner window - note the design's own open question 4 flags this collision). Upgrade the sentinel from 'spec parses' to 'conditions fingerprint == last ACKed fingerprint' per master, so a silent revert or splice is a COURT-class alarm rather than invisible. Add the spec to the workflow's validation gate class.

raw_findings.title: Merge rollback cannot reuse the auto_* machinery, and attempting it silently disables every other demotion in the same pass
raw_findings.attack: Design section 4 says merge rollback is 'the same machinery class as auto_* rollback'. That machinery is sunday_boundary.py:234-236: `for path, old in (av.get('prev') or {}).items(): sect, key = path.split('.'); spec0.setdefault(sect, {})[key] = old`. It is a hardcoded two-level unpack. A master's conditions live three levels deep - `masters.BULL.conditions` - so `path.split('.')` yields three parts and the unpack raises ValueError. That exception is caught by the blanket `except Exception as _de` at 246-247, which wraps the ENTIRE loop over all auto_ markers. Consequence: the first merge marker written in the new format doesn't just fail to roll back itself - it aborts the whole demotion pass, so the exit-knob reverts that work today stop working too, permanently, and the only trace is a single line reading 'demotion check skipped: ValueError'. The ratchet that the anti-cube law depends on quietly stops turning while the boundary telegram still looks normal. Worse for the masters case specifically: the design's rollback semantics are ordinal ('revert the LAST merge only, to prev_conditions'), which the flat path/value prev map cannot express at all - two merges landing between two boundary passes give you no way to restore only the second.
raw_findings.fix: Do not reuse the flat prev map. Build a path-agnostic nested setter and wrap EACH auto_/merge marker in its own try/except so one malformed marker can never mute the others - that per-marker isolation is worth doing regardless of masters, since the current blanket catch is a single point of failure for the whole demotion ratchet. Master rollback restores by merge_history index: pop the head entry, restore its prev_conditions verbatim, assert monotonicity (length decreases by exactly one, restored list equals the recorded prev_conditions byte-for-byte), then restart the evidence clock again for the rollback itself - a rollback is a spec change like any other. Coverage: a MOT/regime-drill fixture that merges a condition and rolls it back and asserts the conditions list round-trips identically; a sentinel check that merge_history head always matches the live conditions. And state the interaction the design leaves open: a rollback during a teacher-frozen proof stint (section 5) must be allowed to fire even though merges are queued, or a degrading master rides out the whole stint - freezing merges and freezing rollbacks are not the same rule.

raw_findings.title: The accrual arithmetic inverts the owner's stated motivation: masters are 1.4x-4x SLOWER per verdict than the probes they replace, and the merge cadence cap guarantees all three masters never complete a verdict window
raw_findings.attack: The court's promotion bar counts SHARED days - days where BOTH the candidate and EXEC_BASELINE traded (scripts/sunday_boundary.py:351-353, `shared = sorted(d for d in dm if d in ctrl_u)`; `if len(shared) < 8`). I measured the control's fill rate from the records: over 2026-08-11..2026-08-25 (11 session days in proactive_sandbox_logs.json) EXEC_BASELINE filled on 8 days = P(control)=0.727; the median probe filled 2-3 days = p_shared 0.09-0.27, i.e. 29-88 trading days to reach 8 shared days. Masters are regime-gated, so their day supply is a strict subset: bull ~50%, mild ~37%, bear ~13% of the calendar (fade_book_spec.json v2.4_note: "bear regimes were ~13% of the last 2 years, so the honest system trades RARELY"; reports/shadow_lab/breaker.jsonl last row: bear_days_2026=20 across 3 episodes). At a generous within-regime fill rate f=0.5, days-to-8-shared are MASTER_BULL 44, MASTER_MILD 59, MASTER_BEAR 169 trading days. The design sets evidence_clock to restart on EVERY merge (§1) and caps merges at 1 per master per month (§3) = ~21 trading days. 21 < 44 < 59 < 169: a master fed merges at the permitted cadence has its clock reset before it can ever accrue 8 shared days. At the cap, three of three masters produce a verdict NEVER, not slower. Second half of the attack: masters do not replace the probe fleet. §3 requires an indicator-probe to pass the full standard bar (>=8 virgin days, trimmed t>=1.8, both halves, floor) BEFORE it can generate a merge proposal. So the 8 priority probes keep running and keep their clocks, and the design adds three more clocked entries that reset on every success. Verdict throughput per quarter falls from ~8 independently-clocked candidates (per-key clocks at sunday_boundary.py:252-257 mean probes no longer reset each other) to 8 + 3-that-never-finish. The owner's core motivation - faster evidence accrual - is not merely unmet, it is reversed by the design's own anti-churn law.
raw_findings.fix: Three changes before any code. (1) Replace the calendar cadence cap with an accrual cap: at most one merge per COMPLETED verdict window per master, and queue proposals at the window boundary rather than monthly. (2) Every merge proposal must publish, from the corpus, the projected post-merge shared-days-to-verdict for that master, and auto-refuse if it exceeds the window the master can actually complete. (3) Refuse to build MASTER_BEAR at all until bear-day supply justifies it - 20 bear days/yr x 0.727 control-fill = ~14 shared bear days per YEAR, so one bear verdict is a ~7-month instrument and one merge restarts it. If the real goal is throughput, the cheap version is already available: the roster is 15 entries (fade_book_spec.json probe.roster) competing for a hard 10-attempt-per-cycle budget (sandbox_proactive_lab.py:2490 `if _att >= 10: break`, plus probe.per_strategy_max_per_day 5 / max_per_day 25). Culling the roster to the priority list raises every survivor's fill rate immediately, with zero new subsystem, zero clock resets, and zero charter friction. Publish the accrual table for both options and let the owner pick against numbers, not intuition.

raw_findings.title: The owner-ACK merge has no ingestion path, no proposal identity, no expiry, and no revalidation — and the one command channel that could carry it replays 24h of updates on state loss
raw_findings.attack: Design §3 says "Owner-ACK telegram required" but no ACK surface exists. scripts/telegram_commands.py:62-106 is the only inbound channel: a `text.startswith` chain over /halt /resume /flatten /cancelflatten /status, authenticated by chat-id equality alone (:79), with its de-dup offset in ~/telegram_commands_state.json and a bare `except: pass` fallback to `{"offset": 0}` (:66-70). Three separate attacks. (a) STALE ACK: the boundary telegrams a proposal on Sunday; the owner ACKs three weeks later. Nothing in the design re-runs the bar. In that window the master's own conditions may have changed, a demotion may have reverted keys (sunday_boundary.py:233-240), and the evidence clock may have restarted — the ACK applies a t-stat earned against a system that no longer exists, which is exactly what the anti-cube law at :248-257 was written to forbid. (b) REPLAY: lose or corrupt the state file (it lives in $HOME on the VPS, is not in the off-box backup set, and any JSON error silently resets it to 0) and getUpdates(offset=1) re-serves every message Telegram still holds — up to 24h. For /halt that is idempotent; for "/ack MERGE-BULL-3" it is a second merge of the same condition, or the re-application of a merge that was already auto-rolled-back. (c) AUTH ASYMMETRY: every command that channel carries today is fail-safe (halt, flatten). ACK is the first PERMISSIVE mutation — a chat-id match now writes new entry conditions into a live master. (d) FREEZE QUEUE: §5 queues merges while a master holds a proof seat, and NORTH_STAR v1.7 pauses the streak on zero-trade weeks — a BEAR master in a bull year can sit mid-stint indefinitely (breaker.jsonl records 20 bear days in all of 2026), so the queue has no bound and its contents rot in place with no age, no expiry, and no re-earn requirement.
raw_findings.fix: Make the proposal a first-class record, not a telegram string: write reports/court/merge_proposals.jsonl with proposal_id, master, condition, the evidence window (exact shared days), spec_version, and a hash of the master's current conditions + the source probe's config. The ACK command carries the id only. On ACK the boundary MUST (1) refuse if proposal_id is already in merge_history (idempotency against replay), (2) refuse if the conditions-hash or spec_version moved since issue, (3) re-run the identical bar on the CURRENT day set and refuse on failure, (4) refuse if age > 7 days (expired, must re-earn). Queued-during-stint merges expire the same way and are re-issued from fresh evidence after the stint, never applied from the stale record. Move the offset state into the harvest-snapshots checkout so it survives, and reject any command older than the poll interval. MOT: replayed ACK is a no-op; stale-hash ACK is refused loudly.

raw_findings.title: "Same machinery class as auto_* rollback" is a claim against machinery that cannot represent a merge — 3-segment paths crash it, date-keyed records overwrite each other, and one bad record silently blinds the whole demotion sweep
raw_findings.attack: Design §4 promises auto-rollback of the last merge "same machinery class as auto_* rollback". Read that machinery. (a) It only ever looks at keys starting with `auto_` (sunday_boundary.py:209) — merge_history entries inside masters.* are invisible to it, so as designed it never runs at all. (b) If you instead write an `auto_` marker to reuse it, the revert does `sect, key = path.split(".")` (:234-236) — a master path like `masters.BULL.conditions` raises ValueError on unpack. That exception is caught by the SINGLE except wrapping the entire demotion block (:246-247), which appends one line, "demotion check skipped: ValueError", and moves on. One malformed record therefore disables demotion for EVERY promoted key in the spec, every week, forever, with the only symptom a type name buried in a long telegram. (c) The record itself is a date-keyed singleton: `spec[f"auto_{date}"]` (:537, :587) and `spec_p[f"promo_{date}"]` (:376). Two merges (three masters, one cadence window) or a merge plus an auto promotion on the same UTC date collide on the dict key — the second silently destroys the first's `prev`/`prev_conditions`, and an un-recorded prior state is an un-rollbackable one. (d) The probe-court class this design borrows from has NO demotion path today: the demotion loop scans `auto_` keys only, so nothing ever re-checks a `promo_*` entry — probe.promoted is read only by sunday_boundary itself (:146, :301) and by no engine code. (e) Every apply commits with `git pull -q --rebase -X ours` (:245, :382, :545, :594): during a rebase "ours" is the upstream side, so a conflicting hunk in fade_book_spec.json resolves in favour of origin and silently DISCARDS the local merge — while `applied[]` and the "MERGE APPLIED" telegram both assert it landed. The court's record and the engine's reality diverge with no alarm.
raw_findings.fix: Do not reuse auto_*. Give merges their own store (masters.X.merge_history, append-only, monotone integer merge_id, never date-keyed) and their own rollback routine with its own tests. raw_findings.title: Merge cadence (1/month) is faster than a master's evidence accrual, so masters are structurally un-judgeable — and a throughput-killing merge can never be auto-rolled-back because rollback requires the trades the merge prevented
raw_findings.attack: The court pairs a strategy against EXEC_BASELINE on SHARED days and needs >=8 (sunday_boundary.py:352). In the live log the control has produced 8 distinct fill days EVER — 2026-08-13 through 2026-08-25 — and ZERO in the fifteen days since. Now impose §1's law that the evidence clock restarts on every merge, at a cadence of 1 merge per master per month. The master needs ~8 shared control days per verdict; the control has historically produced ~8 per two weeks at its best and 0 recently; a BEAR master accrues only on bear days (20 in all of 2026 per breaker.jsonl, ~13% of days per the spec's v2.4_note). A monthly merge therefore restarts the clock before the window can close: the BEAR and probably MILD masters never reach a verdict, never demote, never promote, and never earn a proof seat, while accumulating conditions that were never tested as a set. The anti-churn law becomes an anti-evidence law. Worse, the rollback that is supposed to catch this is structurally unreachable: a merged condition that is too narrow (or whose whitelisted path is never populated in md/candidate) drives the master's fills to zero, so it generates no rows in proactive_sandbox_logs.json, so `shared` never reaches 8 (:352-353 prints "HOLD" forever) and the auto_ demotion analogue never reaches its len(dif)>=10 (:233). A merge that silently kills a master's throughput is permanent until a human notices. Note the MENU path has a CHAMPION fallback precisely so a promoted book's stream cannot go structurally blind (:220-227) — the probe/master path has no equivalent. The 1/month cap is also gamed by ordering, not evidence: the promote loop iterates `for st_ in prio` (:335) and, unlike the MENU apply branches (:528, :576 `if not applied`), has no one-per-run guard — with two same-regime probes passing on the same Sunday, position in probe.priority decides which condition enters the master and which waits a month with rotting evidence.
raw_findings.fix: Gate cadence on EVIDENCE, not the calendar: no merge into a master until it has accrued >=N judgeable shared units since its last merge AND reached a published verdict, with the count regime-eligible (bear days for BEAR). Print per-master "judgeable units since last merge / units to verdict" in every boundary report so a stalled master is visible, never inferred. Add a THROUGHPUT FLOOR for masters mirroring :136-177 — a master whose fills fall to zero for K sessions after a merge auto-reverts that merge without needing a t-test (absence of trades is the evidence). Add a CHAMPION-style fallback stream so a master's court can never go blind. When two proposals target one master, rank by trimmed t (published), never by list order, and cap explicitly per run.

raw_findings.title: The bar certifies a whole probe; the merge transfers only its predicate — and the promote branch has no evidence-clock filter, so the master's post-merge t-stat silently pools two different strategies
raw_findings.attack: Two independent honesty failures in §4's "a merged condition-set is a NEW cohort". (1) UNIT MISMATCH. The design's merge unit is a data predicate over candidate/md. But the anchors it names do not live in their predicate. DIP_CONF_MILD's measured edge is explicitly "the EXPENSIVE trigger contracts" and the live probe buys the trigger contract itself via _PROBE_CONTRACT (sandbox_proactive_lab.py:2507-2510) from a separate pool, _PRICEY_CANDS[:14] (:2483); DIP_CONVEXITY carries its own structure and wide exits (PROBE_STRUCT/PROBE_EXITS, :410-412) plus a hoisted market-level SPY<20d gate (:2478-2481). A probe that clears t>=1.8 clears it as pool + contract selection + structure + exits + predicate. Merging the predicate alone imports the part of the strategy that was never tested in isolation, into a master whose pool/contract/exit context is different — the evidence does not cover the change, and §2's "day one changes no behavior" seed-equivalence cannot hold for those anchors either, since their identity is not expressible as whitelisted path predicates. (2) NO CLOCK IN THIS COURT. The MENU loop filters days by the evidence clock (`d["day"] > _ck`, :476-478, helper at :283-288). The probe-promotion branch does not: by_strat is built from every record in the log (:302-316) and `shared` is unfiltered (:352). So "the clock restarts on merge" is currently unimplementable for masters without new code, and if it is not written, the master's diff series spans pre- and post-merge days against an unchanged control — a mixture presented as one cohort. Compounding it, `if st_ in promoted: continue` (:336) means a master, once promoted, is never re-judged at all, so §4's "masters are judged like any probe" stops the moment it matters.
raw_findings.fix: Merge the TESTED unit or nothing: a proposal must carry every dimension the probe's evidence was earned on (pool selector, contract override, structure, exits) or the bar must be re-earned by a predicate-only variant of the probe running as its own roster slot first. Pre-register which dimensions are mergeable and refuse the rest. Wire a per-master evidence clock into the promote branch keyed on masters.X.conditions and drop days <= last merge date from `shared` (mirror :476-478), with a MOT proving pre-merge days are excluded. Stop skipping promoted masters — continued judging IS the demotion watch that §4 depends on; skip only the re-promotion action, not the evaluation.

raw_findings.title: Seat path and merge path fire off the SAME court pass, so one probe's eight days can both seat it on Proof and rewrite a master — and a queued merge applied after a passed stint mutates the config that just unlocked real money
raw_findings.attack: The proof build contract pins seating to exactly one place: "SEATING fires EXCLUSIVELY in the probe-court PROMOTE branch" (proof_account_build_contract_2026-09-06.md:33-35). §3 of this design generates the merge proposal from the same event in the same branch — "an indicator-probe passing the standard bar". Nothing routes them apart. So one passing probe can (a) take a Proof seat as itself and (b) inject its condition into a master that is itself a natural proof-seat candidate (§5). In a 2-4 seat regime portfolio that is two seats holding correlated entries backed by ONE eight-day sample — the precise thing NORTH_STAR v1.5 forbids ("each earning its seat through the full ladder individually, never riding another's evidence"), and a concentration risk the seat count hides. Second attack: §5 says a queued merge applied after a PASSED stint "restarts the next stint's clock". A passed stint is what unlocks the first real GBP 1-5k under v1.4, with a capture>=60% denominator frozen in writing AT seating (v1.7). Applying the merge afterwards changes the strategy while real capital is staked on it, against a capture denominator now measuring a config that no longer exists — and by this design's own §4 the merged master is a NEW cohort with no inherited t-stats, so the real money is riding an unproven configuration whose only evidence is the stint the OLD configuration earned. Third: the freeze covers merges but not rollbacks. If a master is seated after a merge, the auto-rollback of that merge is the one mutation path left open mid-stint — it silently changes the seated config, splits the stint across two configurations, and neither fails the stint nor restarts it.
raw_findings.fix: Pre-register an exclusive routing rule evaluated BEFORE the bar: a probe is declared either a seat candidate or a merge source at the time it enters probe.priority, never both, recorded in the spec. A master that takes a proof seat freezes ALL mutation, rollback included — if the court wants to roll back a merge on a seated master, that unseats it (contract item 8 machinery: flatten next day, zero rising_weeks, seat_history record, fresh court case), it does not quietly edit a live stint. Any merge into a master that holds a rung ends the rung's authority: back to a fresh stint with a newly frozen capture denominator before any real-money size resumes, stated in writing as a NORTH_STAR-level rule since it spends the owner's cap. And publish, in the weekly report, the correlation between seated strategies' conditions so two seats sharing a merged predicate are visible as one bet.

raw_findings.title: The merge clock is a dilemma, not a design: as specified it never exists in code (verdict laundering), and as written it makes every master permanently unjudged
raw_findings.attack:
Design §1/§4 rests on 'evidence_clock restarts on every merge' and 'the master re-earns from its restarted clock'. Neither half survives contact.

(a) THE CLOCK DOES NOT EXIST ON THIS PATH. The anti-cube clock (_clock, scripts/sunday_boundary.py:283-288) is applied to MENU shadow books ONLY, at scripts/sunday_boundary.py:477 (`and d["day"] > _ck`). The probe court - the machinery the design says masters are judged by - builds day-means from proactive_sandbox_logs.json with NO clock filter at all (scripts/sunday_boundary.py:302-321, 335-370): `shared = sorted(d for d in dm if d in ctrl_u)` is all-time. It also only sees markers written as spec `auto_*` keys (scripts/sunday_boundary.py:264-273), and a merge writes masters.BULL.conditions, not an auto_ marker. So ship the design as drafted and merges restart nothing: a master that merges 'premium>100k' on day 12 is judged on a window whose first 11 days are fills the new condition would have EXCLUDED. The court credits a merge for returns it did not produce - textbook evidence laundering, and the exact failure the anti-cube law was written to stop (scripts/sunday_boundary.py:248-257).

(b) IMPLEMENT IT PROPERLY AND THE MASTERS DIE OF YOUTH. The bar needs >=8 days SHARED with EXEC_BASELINE (scripts/sunday_boundary.py:351-353). Measured rates from the newest engine log (proactive_sandbox_logs.json, 39 entry days): EXEC_BASELINE fills on 8 of the 9 trading days 08-13..08-25 (0.89 control-present); narrow probes fill ~0.3-0.4 of their eligible days (DP_HEAVY 3 days, QUIET_TAPE 5, FADE_WHALE 1). Regime availability: BEAR = 20 days in 2026 across 3 episodes (reports/shadow_lab/breaker.jsonl, bear_days_2026:20; ~12%, matching the '~13% of the last 2 years' in fade_book_spec.json:193). So MASTER_BULL accrues 0.65*0.35*0.89 ~ 0.19 shared days/day = ~4/month -> ~2 months per verdict. MASTER_BEAR: 0.12*0.35*0.89 ~ 0.037 = ~0.8/month -> ~10 months per verdict, arriving in 3 bursts a year. A cadence cap of 1 merge/master/MONTH is therefore set 2x faster than the fastest master can earn a verdict and 10x faster than the slowest. Every merge zeroes a window that never completes. Consequence: no master ever PASSES, and - because auto-rollback and the demotion watch both need a completed window (scripts/sunday_boundary.py:233 needs 10 MORE post-change days) - no master can ever be rolled back or demoted either. The court is structurally blind to the entity the whole design exists to build, while conditions keep accumulating.
raw_findings.fix: Kill the calendar cadence cap and replace it with an evidence cadence: a master accepts a merge only when its CURRENT condition set has already returned a verdict (PASS/HOLD-with-n>=8 shared days) since the previous merge - merge rate then self-limits to the regime's measured fill rate (~1/quarter BULL, ~1/year BEAR) instead of a fictional month. Second, do not restart clocks at all: because AND-merges are pure filters (see finding 3), log the full predicate vector on every master fill and re-score the new condition set retroactively over the master's own recorded trades. The merged cohort then starts with real n on day one, honestly - no laundering, no youth. Third, if any clock semantics ship, they must be wired into the probe court explicitly (scripts/sunday_boundary.py:335-370 currently has none) and that change must be pre-registered, because silently adding a clock mid-flight re-bars all 8 strategies in probe.priority (fade_book_spec.json:128-137).

raw_findings.title: AND-merge shrinkage compounds against itself - three merges deep the master is unjudgeable, and the narrowing steals the shared attempt budget from the control
raw_findings.attack:
Every merge is restrictive by construction (AND-only, design §3). Three compounding harms, none of which the design bounds:

(1) TIME-TO-VERDICT GROWS AS EVIDENCE SHRINKS. Model MASTER_BULL from its seed (BULL and ticker<20d and calls, sandbox_proactive_lab.py:2372-2375) with three plausible merges of 0.6-0.7 survival each: per-day fill rate falls ~0.35 -> ~0.12, giving 1.4 shared days/month (~5.7 months for 8 days). Worse, fills/day collapses toward 1, so the per-day mean's variance roughly triples and the t-test needs ~3x the days for the same power: ~17 months for a verdict that took ~2 months at seed. The symmetric trim then drops the best AND worst of 8 (scripts/sunday_boundary.py:364), leaving six single-trade days to carry a t>=1.8 bar - that is a lottery, not a court.

(2) MARKET-LEVEL PREDICATES DELETE WHOLE DAYS, NOT TRADES. The whitelisted vocabulary includes md.macro.* and md.regime_stack.* (design §1), which are market-level. The engine already hoists exactly these out of the candidate loop because they kill entire days (sandbox_proactive_lab.py:2478-2481). MASTER_MILD already carries two of them (MILD and SPY<20d, sandbox_proactive_lab.py:2387-2392); one more market-level merge can halve its eligible-day count in a single ACK, and days are the unit the bar counts.

(3) NARROWING ONE MASTER THINS EVERY OTHER STRATEGY'S EVIDENCE. probe_filter is evaluated INSIDE enter_proactive_set, after the sensor sweep, and each non-matching candidate consumes one of the cycle's 10 attempts (sandbox_proactive_lab.py:2464-2467, 2489-2515). This is a documented, already-paid failure: 'rare-filter probes whose pools burn 10 attempts each without entering, cycle time blew past the dispatch interval, and every run from 17:40Z was cancelled by its successor' (sandbox_proactive_lab.py:2456-2463). The code elsewhere states the taboo explicitly - 'thinning the control mid-experiment would quietly change the bar for all tracked strategies' (sandbox_proactive_lab.py:2438-2441). Merging conditions into masters is precisely mid-experiment control thinning, imposed on every other probe through a shared budget, with no accounting anywhere in the design. Finally, the boundary already blocks RESTRICTIVE promotions when throughput breaches (scripts/sunday_boundary.py:140,471) and per-leg starvation is a paging condition (scripts/sunday_boundary.py:161-167) - the merge path inherits neither guard, so it can starve the book in exactly the state the FADE path is forbidden to.
raw_findings.fix: Make throughput a pre-condition of ACK, computed before the telegram: replay the proposed predicate over the master's own last-90-day fills and REFUSE the merge if it removes >30% of them, or if projected fills/eligible-day drops below 1.0, or if the master's projected shared-day rate pushes time-to-verdict past one quarter. Register masters in the per-leg throughput floor (scripts/sunday_boundary.py:155-167) so a starved master pages and auto-blocks further merges, same as any promoted leg. Ban market-level paths (md.macro.*, md.regime_stack.*) from merge predicates entirely - a market-level idea is a REGIME definition, not a condition; it belongs in the regime router where it is priced once, not multiplied into a day filter. And hoist every merged predicate that is candidate-only into the free pre-sweep check beside _CALLS_ONLY (sandbox_proactive_lab.py:2495-2498) so narrowing can never consume the attempt budget the control depends on.

raw_findings.title: Last-merge rollback cannot attribute a failure it did not cause - and stint-queued merges land in batches that make attribution impossible by construction
raw_findings.attack:
Design §4 reverts 'the LAST merge only'. Three ways that misfires:

(1) WRONG SUSPECT. With ~1-3 fills/day over 8 days, a master's day-mean rests on ~10-20 trades where one -70% stop dominates. Merge k-2 can be the poison and merge k the innocent bystander; the machinery reverts k, the master keeps failing, and the next verdict is another ~2-10 months away (finding 1). Serial rollback through three merges costs years of regime days.

(2) BATCHED MERGES BREAK IT OUTRIGHT. Design §5 queues merges during a teacher-frozen proof stint. NORTH_STAR stints run 8 weeks; at 1 merge/master/month that queue holds 2-3 merges applied together on stint exit. 'Roll back the last merge' is then meaningless - three conditions entered as one event, and prev_conditions records only the last hop.

(3) THE ROLLBACK MAY BE JUDGED ON THE WRONG COHORT ANYWAY. The existing demotion watch, when a promoted book's stream vanishes, silently substitutes CHAMPION's returns (scripts/sunday_boundary.py:219-229). Point that machinery at a master whose narrowed condition set stops filling - the most likely post-merge state - and it judges the merge on a stream that is not the master at all. And it needs 10 further post-merge days (scripts/sunday_boundary.py:233): ~10 months of BEAR days for MASTER_BEAR, i.e. a bad bear merge is permanent on any horizon the proof ladder cares about.

The deep point: AND-merges are PURE FILTERS, so a master's trade set after merge k is a strict subset of the set before it. Every counterfactual condition-set is therefore already computable from trades that have already happened - the design throws that away and buys attribution with fresh live months instead.
raw_findings.fix: Log the full predicate vector on every master fill at entry (one record per contract - the record must carry which conditions it passed, evaluated for ALL conditions including ones merged later where computable, plus regime and the tuned exit config in force). Attribution then becomes a table scan: re-score all 2^k subsets of the condition set over the same trades and rank merges by marginal contribution, no new evidence required. Rollback removes the WORST-contributing merge, not the newest. Forbid batch application: on stint exit release exactly one queued merge and drop the rest back to proposals (a merge that cannot be attributed is not evidence). Explicitly bar the CHAMPION substitution for masters - a master with no fills is a THROUGHPUT alarm, never a stream to be silently replaced.

raw_findings.title: Seeding is not information transfer - the predicate vocabulary carries only the filter half, and the measured edge of all three anchors lives in the half that gets dropped
raw_findings.attack:
Design §2 claims masters seeded with their anchors' current conditions 'changes no behavior on day one', and §1 claims 'merges are data commits, never code edits'. Both are false against the code.

(1) THE EDGE IS NOT IN THE CONDITIONS. Every anchor's measured result is inseparable from a name-keyed override that the predicate vocabulary cannot express. DIP_CONVEXITY's edge is bear + LONG-DTE calls + WIDE exits - PROBE_STRUCT otm 2.0/dte 50 and PROBE_EXITS -70/80/0.30 (sandbox_proactive_lab.py:410-412), evidenced as such in fade_book_spec.json:140-149. DIP_CONF_MILD and BULL_DIP_X BUY THE TRIGGER CONTRACT out of the pricey pool via _PROBE_CONTRACT and _PRICEY_CANDS (sandbox_proactive_lab.py:2482-2488, 2507-2510) - the spec calls that the panel-corrected essence of the cell (fade_book_spec.json:155, 161). All of it is keyed by strategy NAME. Rename to MASTER_BEAR and _tuned() finds nothing (sandbox_proactive_lab.py:418-431), PROBE_EXITS has no MASTER_* entry, and the engine silently falls back to the generic defaults stop 50 / trig 50 / give 0.20 (sandbox_proactive_lab.py:1131-1149). Day one therefore changes behaviour in exactly the direction the evidence says destroys the edge - the spec's own note says the -50 stop 'sat inside bear whipsaw range and cost a third of the measured edge'. The seed-equivalence MOT of §6 will not catch this if it tests conditions on fixtures rather than the full entry-to-exit config.

(2) 'DATA COMMITS, NEVER CODE EDITS' IS UNTRUE AT STEP 1. Anchor identities are hardcoded in at least six files: sandbox_proactive_lab.py:410-412, 2372-2392, 2454-2455, 2471-2472, 2478-2488; scripts/glide_sim.py:37-46; scripts/probe_tuner.py:150-152; scripts/tuner_apply.py:36-39; scripts/roadmap_tests.py:144; scripts/trajectory_scoreboard.py:25-26. Retiring anchors is a multi-file code change with a bar-changing side effect on every court that keys off those names.

(3) THE 'ZERO vs INHERIT' QUESTION IS CURRENTLY MOOT AND HIDES A WORSE ONE. In the newest engine log (proactive_sandbox_logs.json, last entry 2026-08-25) NONE of BULL_DIP, DIP_CONVEXITY or DIP_CONF_MILD has a single live fill; they entered the roster 2026-08-27..09-01 (fade_book_spec.json:152,156,162). So the masters would be seeded from entities whose entire record is backtest - one of which carries an explicit sampling-contradiction flag in the spec itself ('may be sampling-sensitive', fade_book_spec.json:161). Presenting them as 'accumulations of everything every probe has proven' is the dishonest part, not the zeroing.
raw_findings.fix: Before step 1, produce the live fill count and shared-day count for each anchor from the VPS log; if an anchor has <8 shared days, it is a hypothesis and the master seeded from it must be labelled UNPROVEN in merge_history, not 'seeded from a proven anchor'. Extend the merge record to the FULL config - conditions AND structure AND exits AND pool routing - and make the seed step copy PROBE_STRUCT/PROBE_EXITS/_PROBE_CONTRACT/pool selection into masters.* explicitly, keyed by master name, with a MOT assertion that engine-resolved (struct, exits, pool, contract-source) for MASTER_X is byte-equal to the anchor's on the same fixture. Where a probe's proven edge cannot be expressed in the merge vocabulary, the merge is REFUSED with 'not representable' - never approved as its filter shadow, which is a different, unmeasured strategy wearing the source probe's t-stat.

raw_findings.title: Three unsynchronised 14-day clocks and three unsynchronised writers on one JSON file: the Friday tuner mutates masters under a running clock and -X ours can silently drop the merge it just announced
raw_findings.attack:
Design §1 routes master exits through probe.tuning, which puts the weekly tuner inside the merge path.

(1) EXIT GLIDES ARE INVISIBLE TO THE ANTI-CUBE LAW. tuner_apply writes probe.tuning.<name>.exits plus its own history and applied stamp (scripts/tuner_apply.py:186-192) and writes NO auto_* marker. The boundary builds key_chg/blanket_chg/frozen_keys exclusively from auto_* keys (scripts/sunday_boundary.py:264-279). So every Friday glide - up to 15% of the gap per knob, or a full JUMP on drama (scripts/tuner_apply.py:175-180) - changes the strategy while its evidence clock keeps running. For masters this is fatal to the design's central claim: the merge path carefully restarts a clock that the tuner then invalidates twice per merge cycle, unrecorded. Verdicts get earned against a configuration that no longer exists - the precise thing scripts/sunday_boundary.py:248-251 forbids.

(2) THREE COOLDOWNS THAT CANNOT SEE EACH OTHER. tuner cooldown is per-strategy on tuning[s]['applied'], 14d (scripts/tuner_apply.py:147-151); boundary cooldown is per spec-key-path, 14d (scripts/sunday_boundary.py:274-279, 468-470); the design adds a third 14d merge cooldown on a namespace neither knows. A merge ACK'd on Saturday is followed by an exit glide on the next Friday, six days inside its cooldown, on the same entity. Also note masters.* is not in LIVE_WIRED (scripts/sunday_boundary.py:518-522), so the boundary's own 'refuse to promote a key the engine does not read' guard has no opinion about merge conditions - the merge path bypasses the audit that exists because of the trail-keys-never-read breakdown (BREAKDOWNS.md:219-224).

(3) THE WRITE PATH CAN LOSE THE MERGE AND KEEP THE RECEIPT. fade_book_spec.json is rewritten wholesale (indent=1) and pushed by at least three processes - scripts/sunday_boundary.py:243-245,380-382,543-545,592-594; scripts/tuner_apply.py:196-199; scripts/engine_failover_exits.py:57 - all using `git pull -q --rebase -X ours`, which during a rebase resolves conflicting hunks to the UPSTREAM side and silently discards the local edit, while the engine box pulls the same file with `-X theirs` (scripts/engine_watch.sh:58,75,104). Friday tuner and the nightly/Sunday boundary write in the same window. A dropped hunk means the ACK telegram fires and merge_history records a condition the live spec does not contain - and worse, a later prev_conditions is captured relative to a state that lost an earlier merge, so rollback restores a condition set that never traded. That is a merge_history that no longer describes any real cohort.
